headline: Last session: Indian indices traded cautiously amid Middle East tensions and concerns over upcoming public sector bank strikes.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Geopolitical risks escalated following drone and missile attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.
Investor caution ahead of a planned three-day strike by public sector bank employees.
Warnings of potential cyberattacks and disruptions in the nascent semiconductor ecosystem.
Internal boardroom tensions at Tata Sons weighing on sentiment for group stocks.
whatHappening: Finance Ministry is convening a meeting with PSB and RRB chiefs to ensure banking continuity.
Tiruppur yarn producers are lobbying garment units to help modify the role of the CCI.
Aviation safety bodies are seeking a comprehensive evaluation of Boeing 787 electrical systems.
International diplomatic friction is rising as Iran threatens to exit the nuclear treaty.

summary: The Indian market is closed today for the weekend following a session marked by global geopolitical instability and domestic labor concerns. The Finance Ministry is actively working to prevent banking disruptions scheduled for next week, while the semiconductor sector faces new security warnings. Investors remain focused on corporate governance at Tata Sons and the evolving situation in the Middle East.
